rulings.model: The text says a registered domestic partner in these states 'must generally report half the combined community income' but states no exception for joint filers. The pages given do not show whether this gate's 'not filing jointly' condition is correct; Form 8958 and Pub. 555 would be needed.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; i1040gi p. 23, Community Property States: "Nevada, Washington, and California domestic partners. A registered domestic partner in Nevada, Washington, or California must generally report half the combined community income of the individual and their domestic partner. See Form 8958 and Pub. 555." The model asks whether the gate's 'not filing jointly' condition is right and says the pages given do not decide it. What decides it is p501 p. 6, not among the pages given (the render had p501 p. 9 only): "Individuals who have entered into a registered domestic partnership, civil union, or other similar relationship that isn't denominated as a marriage under the law of the state ... aren't lawfully married for federal tax purposes", and a joint return requires that "You were married at the end of 2025" or that your spouse died in 2025 (i1040gi p. 13, Married Filing Jointly). A joint filer is therefore filing with a spouse, not a domestic partner, and the joint return already reports both spouses' combined income; the partner rule reaches a partner on a single, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse return, which is where the gate refuses (the separate married-filing-separately refusal, s3.mfs, covers the remaining status). The restatement (status not mfj, community property state, registered domestic partner) is otherwise the source's condition. The line is unchanged since fix round 2, where it was checked against p. 23, p525 p. 24 and p501 p. 6. Project stands.
